traits: Pale green to verdigris cap on a cream background, 5 to 12 cm, dry, cracking into small polygonal patches
Cream-white, brittle gills, sometimes spotted rusty brown
White stem, 4 to 8 cm, thick, brittle, no ring and no volva
Thick, brittle white flesh · mild, nutty taste
Broadleaf woods, warm places, edges · July to October
safetyNote: The cracked, patchy cap, the flesh that snaps like chalk, and the absence of ring and volva set it apart from the death cap, which is smooth, has a ring and a volva, and whose flesh does not snap. The green form of the death cap is sometimes mistaken for a russula (Belgian poison centre).
